title: "Install animovement"
description: "Install the animovement ecosystem from r-universe, load it, and add the optional packages."
order: 1
---

## Install the ecosystem {#sec-install}

*animovement* is distributed through
[r-universe](https://animovement.r-universe.dev). Installing the `animovement`
metapackage pulls in the whole ecosystem — the core packages you need for a
complete movement-analysis workflow:

```r
install.packages(
  "animovement",
  repos = c(
    "https://animovement.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)
```

The second repository (`cloud.r-project.org`, i.e. CRAN) is there so that any
dependencies that don't live on r-universe are found too.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Only need one piece?
Every package installs the same way — just swap `"animovement"` for the
individual package name:

```r
install.packages(
  "aniread",
  repos = c(
    "https://animovement.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)
```

See [Packages](../packages/index.qmd) for the full list of what each package does.
:::

## Load it {#sec-load}

Load the metapackage to bring the full workflow into scope. Like the tidyverse,
`library(animovement)` attaches the core packages in one call:

```r
library(animovement)
```

From here on, the guides assume you've run this.

## Optional (suggested) packages {#sec-suggested}

Some functions rely on extra packages that aren't installed by default — for
example, particular file readers or smoothing methods. Install all of these
*suggested* packages in one go with:

```r
install_suggested_packages()
```

You can always install them later; *animovement* will tell you which package a
function needs if it's missing.
